text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 1739991234 detected: elevated 5xx and GPU OOMs across serving-runtime pool eu-west-1c. Paging oncall now.
ling (oncall): seeing steady stream of `OOMKilled` + `cuda:unknown error` in runtime pods, autoscaler spiking nodes from 12 -> 48 in ~3m then back down. nodes flapping.
maya (sre): confirmed. a lot of pods entering CrashLoopBackOff after scale up. kubelet `eviction` events + dockerd restarting on some hosts.
sam (runtime eng): stack from one crashed pod:```
2026-03-10T12:03:07Z runtime[pid:1]: memory exceed, OOMKilled
[libnvvp] ERROR: cuda: device-side assert triggered
Traceback (most recent call last): RuntimeError: CUDA unknown error
```
jordan (platform): autoscaler logs show aggressive scaling due to CPU thresh oscillation; policy cooldowns set to 10s for burst policy. looks like a feedback loop: more nodes -> more pods -> more KV cache warming -> memory blowout -> pods restart -> metrics spike -> scale.
ling (oncall): customer impact: increased tail latency and ~15% 5xx for model-serving endpoints. support tickets stacking. @nora any customer-facing notes?
nora (support): posting to status: short message drafted, recommending retry/backoff for SDK users. adding incident banner for impacted regions.
maya (sre): immediate mitigation plan: 1) pause autoscaler burst policy, 2) pin desired node count to stable pool (12), 3) cordon and drain 2 most-unstable machines, 4) scale down replicas for heavy KV models to reduce memory footprint.
sam (runtime eng): agree. also revert last runtime image roll (deployed ~20m before incident) — that image contained an unbounded cache change. initiating rollback now.
incidents-bot: @oncall ling acknowledged. Handoff to sampager in 5m if not resolved.
jordan (platform): disabling burst autoscaling: `kubectl patch configmap cluster-autoscaler -p '{"data":{"burst_enabled":"false"}}'` -> applied. set `--max-node-provision-time=10m` to avoid rapid churn.
ling (oncall): cordoning two noisy nodes: `kubectl cordon ip-10-0-7-23` / `kubectl drain ip-10-0-7-23 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`
maya (sre): observed memory usage drop after rollback and cordon. CrashLoopBackOffs decreasing. Crash logs now show kernel OOM messages correlate with dockerd restarts.
sam (runtime eng): heap snapshot suggests cache size multiplied by factor ~4 under new image when multiple workers spawned. backporting fix to runtime to cap cache per-worker.
ling (oncall): note: autoscaler metrics lag ~30s; manual intervention required while rollback propagates.
jordan (platform): temporarily reduced deployment replica count for heavy-model-service: `kubectl scale deploy heavy-model-service --replicas=4` (was 16) -> rolled out.
nora (support): customers from a handful of enterprise tenants reported degraded throughput; set expectation: mitigation in progress, updates every 15m.
maya (sre): creating short-lived admission webhook to limit new heavy pods per node? risky. alternative: set `maxUnavailable` on rollout to avoid spike.
sam (runtime eng): patch merged in PR #4021, CI green, rolling restart plan: controlled restart with `rollingUpdate.maxSurge=0` and manual pod-by-pod restart.
incidents-bot: Deploy bot: rollback of runtime image completed at 1739991298 by sam (runtime eng).
ling (oncall): monitoring: 5xx rate trending down, OOM events falling. still seeing two hosts with kernel panics earlier, investigating hardware flakiness.
jordan (platform): raised node hardware alert to infra: possible NVLINK driver causing driver resets under memory pressure. filing a ticket with host provider.
nora (support): updated status: 'Partial degradation in EU-West. Mitigation underway. Next update in 15 minutes.' :white_check_mark:
maya (sre): proposed postmortem action items: - tighten autoscaler cooldowns and add damping (hysteresis) - add pre-scaling health probe: only add nodes if existing pod restarts < 1/min - default per-pod memory caps for heavy-model containers - fail-open circuit to fallback small-quant model on OOM surge
sam (runtime eng): also adding regression test simulating KV cache warmup under scale-up to perf-eval harness.
ling (oncall): handoff to maya for long-term mitigation. maya, you're owning PM. I'm staying to support for 15m.
maya (sre): ack. creating incident channel notes and assigning owners.
incidents-bot: On-call handoff: ling -> maya at 1739991360.
ling (oncall): final note before handoff: watch for autoscaler re-enable — keep burst disabled until postmortem.
jordan (platform): set autoscalerBurst flag = false in infra config repo and opened PR to make it a gated change behind feature-flag.
nora (support): prepping customer follow-up summary after incident ends.
maya (sre): summary: immediate mitigations applied (rollback, autoscaler burst disabled, drain unstable nodes, scale down heavy services). Observed recovery: 5xx down to baseline, OOM events minimal. Next steps: root-cause deep dive, runbook updates, and deploy new runtime with bounded cache + test harness. ETA for full RCA: 72h.
ling (oncall): thanks team. closing paging for oncall rotation. leaving channel open for follow-ups. :thumbsup:
